scope.description: Four cases as in the previous revision - a ConfigurationStore-only control and three dual-interface cases triggered by a voter address change, an AddNonvoter and a RemoveServer - each reporting the StoreConfiguration and ApplyBatch configuration counts, with the setup event now carrying the same trigger identifier as the result event so the admission can be matched.
assumptions: All three commands are legal on a three-voter cluster, as before.
The setup and result events now share batching_fsm and trigger, which is the identity the comparisons use.
The recorder is still shared across the cluster's FSMs.
excluded: DemoteVoter and the deprecated Promote command.

basis.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with three peers, bootstrapping and the in-memory test configuration, and a MakeFSMFunc returning either an FSM implementing FSM and ConfigurationStore or one that also implements ApplyBatch, all recording into a shared recorder. The case emits assurance_config_store_setup with the batching flag, the trigger name, the leader and target identities and the peer count, issues exactly one configuration command according to the trigger (AddVoter with a new address for the target voter, AddNonvoter for a fresh identity, or RemoveServer of the target follower), waits up to five seconds for a callback counter to become non-zero, waits a further 200ms, and emits assurance_config_store_result with the same trigger and batching flags plus the command's error and the counts. The harness is TestAssuranceConfigurationStoreWithBatching.

comparisons.description: Dual-interface FSM after an AddNonvoter: whether the documented callback arrives.
Dual-interface FSM after a RemoveServer: whether the documented callback arrives.
The standing dual-interface case, re-measured with the others.
Control: the ConfigurationStore-only FSM receives the callback.

before.description: Four cases, each a three-voter cluster built with the repository's own helper whose FSMs share a recorder: a ConfigurationStore-only FSM with a voter address change as the control, and three dual-interface FSMs whose single configuration change is a voter address change, an AddNonvoter, or a RemoveServer of a follower. Each case reports the StoreConfiguration and ApplyBatch configuration counts together with the command's result.
assumptions: All three commands are legal on a three-voter cluster: moving a voter's address keeps three voters, AddNonvoter adds a non-voter, and removing one follower leaves two voters, which is still a quorum.
Each case produces exactly one committed configuration entry, so the counts are comparable across cases.
As before, the recorder is shared across the cluster's FSMs so the counts answer whether the callback fires anywhere.
excluded: DemoteVoter and the deprecated Promote/AddStaging commands, and any multi-command sequence.

revision_reason: The previous revision added two triggers but emitted the setup event without the trigger field, so the identity built from batching_fsm and trigger could not be matched and all four comparisons came back unresolved. This revision adds trigger to the setup event; cases, counters and comparisons are otherwise identical.
